scope: Q04 observation only:8 healthy condition rows plus8 observer-off controls
decision: Earliest post-drag target reversal occurs in held and released inputs before home-return. Common follow-through decay causes aimRaw reversal at.55s and filtered aim/wrist rate reversal at.725s. Release-specific home return begins.8s and changes mapped targets only.825/.833333s. No new candidate adopted.

protocol.preparation: Legacy3s, pairedmeasurement; drag.55s; ending1.2s; seed7; actual G.step/native unchanged.
protocol.controlTime: pre-physics timestamp; skill update already complete. Skill recovery writes handOffset AFTER aimRaw/filter in that frame, so aim responds next step.
protocol.torque: Controller component requests before Hill/cap plus actual applied vectors separately. No counterfactual component work; path signed midpoint work includes recorded reaction bodies.
protocol.angularVelocity: Shoulder targetRelativeOmega is parent-relative rate expressed in world; targetWorldOmegaApprox adds actual pre-step parent omega. Wrist targetOmega is the existing world target cross-product rate projected perpendicular to current blade. Actual rates recorded before physics and after physics.
protocol.limits: No intervention/return/cap/gain changes; only unopposed healthy strokes. No native total work or human/mobile verdict.

interpretation: At control.55s swing classification becomes false, capped follow±.105m decays to±.102123m and aimRaw reverses while handOffset/anchor remain at drag endpoint. This is common in hold/release.
The first wrist reversal at.725s is paired with identical aimVel reversal in all four pairs; handHeld does not freeze filtered/follow targets.

Longsword down shoulder relative reversal at.658333s contains relative−.004780 and parent+.043781rad/s on same stroke axis, leaving world desired+.039001. It is therefore not itself a reversal of desired world motion. Other first shoulder reversals have mixed geometry/body contributions.

Return increases wrist target-rate and explicit wrist positive net path work in several windows; paired automatic-return output differences are measured, but no total brake/efficiency claim is available.
Upper-arm up-hold target rates can be large while filtered aim barely moves; coupled IK/body feedback is an independent issue and cannot be reduced to wrist automatic-return.

nextMinimalImplementationTarget.proposal: A future isolated hold-endpoint latch: when actual drag ends with handHeld=true and swinging=false, keep the current follow contribution/aimRaw endpoint until next deliberate input or recovery rather than silently retracting it. Implement only in a temporary module, preserve actual torque budgets, compare first2matched down/up holdconditions. No implementation in this diagnosis.
nextMinimalImplementationTarget.reason: All4pairs share a measured .55→.725s recoil before any release-only home return; changing shoulder zero-twist damping did not fix it. The input-layer follow transition is the earliest causal path shared by both controllers.
nextMinimalImplementationTarget.limits: Must verify reachability and restart continuity; a latch does not establish whole-body transfer or fix high upper-arm target angular rates in up holds. No gain tuning or broad candidate release.
